name: capell-app/widget-location-map
description: A numbered list of up to twenty places with addresses and OpenStreetMap links, plus a map that loads on request.

marketplace.summary: Your offices or branches listed with addresses and map links, and an OpenStreetMap view only when a visitor asks.
marketplace.description: List up to twenty offices or branches on a page built in Layout Builder, each numbered with its name, an optional address and a link to OpenStreetMap. You enter each place's latitude and longitude by hand. A button below the list loads an interactive map, and nothing comes from OpenStreetMap until a visitor presses it. The map frames every place and marks one only when the list has a single place. If Privacy Centre is on and a visitor has refused OpenStreetMap, they see a short note in place of the map.
marketplace.problem: I want visitors to find our places, but a map that loads for everyone slows the page.
marketplace.outcome: Every address comes with a map link, and the interactive map loads on one click.

faq.question: What do visitors see before the map loads?
faq.answer: A list of your places, up to twenty, each with its name, an address if you gave one and a link that opens OpenStreetMap at that spot. Nothing is requested from OpenStreetMap until a visitor presses Load interactive map.

faq.question: Which places appear on the interactive map?
faq.answer: The map opens on an area wide enough to take in every place in your list. A pin marks the spot only when the list holds a single place, so with several places visitors see the area without pins.

faq.question: Can visitors search by postcode?
faq.answer: No. For each place you enter a latitude and a longitude, which you can copy from a map app.

faq.question: What if a visitor has declined cookies?
faq.answer: If your site runs Privacy Centre and they turned down functional cookies, pressing the button shows a short note and no map loads. The list and its links work for everyone either way.
